title: A quarter of the longer words on a page were already written on that page
statement: In paragraph text, at least a quarter (0.25) of the certain words of four or more glyphs were already written earlier on the same page.
source: F-009 says only that this share beats words dealt across pages; it sets no level, so a generator passes it with far less reuse than the manuscript has. This registers the level. Public practice split (Zandbergen-Landini): 0.311 on the evaluation pages; Takahashi 0.307, RF 0.294. Twelve random samples of 34 training pages give 0.266 to 0.317 and six systematic ones (every sixth page) 0.272 to 0.304; the line is at 0.25 because the share depends on page length and on which pages are drawn. Against language, for context only (no reference comparison is registered, since the references are continuous texts and their topical locality is not comparable): of 44 reference languages poured into the layout of the evaluation pages, one (Vietnamese, 0.42) is above the manuscript and the next are Dutch 0.29, Danish 0.28, Norwegian 0.27; the median is far lower. So heavy within-page reuse of whole words is unusual but not unknown in ordinary text. Why it is a useful target: together with the singleton share sent under K-001-open-2 (at least two word types in three occur once; manuscript 0.71) it forms a pincer. On the practice split the line-chain generator with a drifting table and copies of recent words gives, when 3 copies in 10 are exact, reuse 0.26 to 0.30 (passes) but singleton share 0.58 to 0.65 (fails); when 1 copy in 20 is exact, singleton share 0.68 to 0.71 (passes) but reuse 0.21 to 0.24 (fails). A one-table chain gives reuse 0.20 to 0.21. The manuscript repeats whole words on a page as often as the first setting while keeping as many once-only words as the second: its repeats fall on few, common words. No procedure tried here does both.
